title: Indirect thermosyphon data cooling
summary: Munters launched SyCool ITC, a 250 kW packaged indirect thermosyphon dry-cooling unit for data centres that uses waste heat and gravity to drive the refrigeration cycle without pumps or compressors. Munters claims it is the first pump-free system to market, with zero water use; no test data are given.
thermal: Pump-free indirect thermosyphon heat rejection for data halls.
manufacturing: Packaged air-handling unit; no build or test details.

title: HFO refrigerant-ready indirect thermosyphon cooling for data centres
summary: Syndicated note on the same 250 kW indirect thermosyphon unit, described as HFO-ready, oil-free and water-free, with a compressor loop for hot days. Energy-saving statements are unquantified claims.
thermal: Two-phase thermosyphon loop with compressor assist at high ambient.

title: Characterization of a Rack-Level Thermosyphon-Based Cooling System
summary: Villanova University and Seguente characterised a pilot rack-level thermosyphon on a 42U rack using R1233zd(E), an air-cooled evaporator and water-cooled condenser. It ran stably from 2 to 7.5 kW, with minimum thermosyphon resistance 6.8 mK/W at 5.7 kW, maximum evaporator pressure drop 21.5 kPa and a 25-minute time constant. Energy balances closed within 15%.
thermal: Passive refrigerant thermosyphon removing 2-7.5 kW of rack heat with no pump.
manufacturing: Pilot rack build with finned-tube evaporator; authors say line sizes should shrink in the next prototype.

title: British Patient Capital invests £5 million in immersion cooling technology business Iceotope
summary: British Patient Capital put £5m into Sheffield's Iceotope as part of a £30m Series B led by ABC Impact, with nVent, SDCL, Northern Gritstone, Pavilion Capital and Edinv. Performance statements are company claims with no data.
thermal: Chassis-level precision liquid cooling for IT equipment.

title: Waste Heat from Data Centres: a Strategic Review for Scotland
summary: Scottish Enterprise commissioned AECOM and HermeticaBlack to review data-centre heat reuse in Scotland, focused on district heat networks, from desk research, interviews and case studies. It says one large data centre could yield hundreds of GWh of recoverable heat a year, and recommends favouring closed-loop over high-water-use evaporative cooling.
thermal: Heat recovery into heat networks; recommends closed-loop cooling designed for reuse.

title: Waste heat from data centres could heat over 3.5 million UK homes
summary: Republished article on EnergiRaven and Viegand Maagøe research projecting enough data-centre waste heat for at least 3.5 million UK homes by 2035, if heat networks are built. No method is given.
thermal: Data-centre waste heat into heat networks.

title: Data centres urged to reuse waste heat for housing
summary: Power On, a utility connections provider, urges UK data-centre developers to supply nearby homes and offices with recovered heat, arguing it helps planning and adds revenue. It notes heat recovery is still uncommon in the UK. Advocacy, no figures.
thermal: Heat recovery into district heating with heat pumps.

title: Advanced Aerospace Heat Exchanger Design, Performance and Manufacturing
publisher: EPSRC CDT in Future Fluid Dynamics, University of Leeds
summary: A Leeds PhD project with BAE Systems Warton plans to model two-phase aircraft heat exchangers (evaporators and condensers), demonstrate design enhancements made by additive layer manufacturing, and generate early design options by simulation. BAE offers manufacturing facilities that may build and test proof-of-concept demonstrators. Plan only, undated.
thermal: Single- and two-phase heat exchangers for aircraft thermal management.
manufacturing: Proposed AM demonstrators tested at BAE Systems.

title: Novel heat exchanger design and sizing methods for Future Advanced Aircraft
publisher: EPSRC CDT in Future Fluid Dynamics, University of Leeds
summary: A follow-on Leeds PhD project with BAE Systems aims at fast models for sizing single-phase, two-phase and phase-change-material heat exchangers that handle mission-system waste heat, runnable on a laptop rather than an HPC cluster. Plan only, undated.
thermal: Fast sizing of aircraft heat exchangers including phase-change material.

title: Flow-priority optimization of additively manufactured variable-TPMS lattice heat exchanger based on macroscopic analysis
summary: Waseda University and AGC optimised the local wall threshold of a TPMS Primitive lattice to balance hot and cold flows in a two-fluid counterflow heat exchanger, using a fast Darcy-Forchheimer model. The optimum was printed in 316L by laser powder bed fusion (0.5 mm minimum wall) and tested with water; measured heat transfer averaged 28.7% better than a uniform lattice.
thermal: Graded TPMS two-fluid heat exchanger, measured against a uniform lattice.

title: Optimization of Higher-Order Harmonic Surface Tessellations for Additively Manufactured Air-to-Air Heat Exchangers
summary: University of the District of Columbia researchers optimised a second-order harmonic surface for air-to-air heat exchangers with a surrogate model coupled to COMSOL. They report up to 70% higher effectiveness with more pressure drop, and that the shape beats a gyroid in turbulent flow (Re above 7000). Simulation only; one reported effectiveness value above 1 needs checking. DOE-funded.

orgs.name: University of the District of Columbia

thermal: Air-air heat-exchanger surface optimisation versus gyroid.

title: Design and fabrication of a TPMS-based micro heat exchanger via micro selective laser melting
summary: Laserinstitut Hochschule Mittweida built three gyroid micro heat exchangers by micro selective laser melting with features down to 100 µm and compared them with a microchannel unit. The abstract reports heat transfer coefficients up to 12 kW/(m²K), over 300% higher than conventional plate heat exchangers, and leak-free operation to 8 bar.
thermal: Gyroid micro heat exchangers up to 12 kW/(m²K).
manufacturing: Micro-SLM with 100 µm features; leak-tested to 8 bar.

title: A novel fabrication method for polymeric flat plate pulsating heat pipe via additive manufacturing
summary: University of Brighton and University of Pavia printed flat-plate pulsating heat pipes in plastic by stereolithography (185 x 85 x 2 mm, eight turns, FC-72 at 50% fill). Thermal resistance fell from 2.5 to 1.7 °C/W over 5-30 W, an effective conductivity over a thousand times that of the solid plastic.

title: Experimental characterization of the effect of acceleration on the performance of additively manufactured loop heat pipes using infrared thermography
summary: The von Karman Institute plans to test loop heat pipes with additively manufactured porous evaporators under up to 2g acceleration with infrared thermography, in the Skywin-funded LHP4ebox project for electronics boxes. No results yet.
thermal: AM-wick loop heat pipes under acceleration.
manufacturing: AM porous evaporator; IR thermography test rig planned.

title: Addireen scales green laser AM manufacturing for copper thermal management
summary: Addireen opened a plant in Ganzhou able to build up to 50 green-laser metal AM systems a month. Its dual 532 nm XH-M350G-2HR prints pure copper at up to 24.24 cm³/h, with stated density up to 99.9% and conductivity up to 400 W/(m·K); these are company figures without a test report. Cold plates and heat exchangers are the target.
thermal: Pure copper cold plates and heat exchangers.

title: Overcoming the Challenges of Copper
summary: 2017 trade article on Fraunhofer ILT's green laser for copper SLM and Protiq copper induction coils. Electrical figures only.
manufacturing: Green-laser SLM of copper in development.
gate_reason: No thermal content; old and superseded by current green-laser copper news.
